name: Form
description: A react-hook-form integration layer. FormField provides context; FormItem generates ids; FormControl wires aria-describedby and aria-invalid; FormMessage renders the error.
intent: Wires a control to its label, description and error message so the accessibility relationships are correct by construction.

authority.note: src/ is authoritative. If this contract disagrees with the source, implement from the source and report the drift.

parts.name: FormField
parts.note: Provides the react-hook-form Controller and field name context

parts.name: FormItem
parts.note: Generates the id namespace that ties label, control, description and message together

parts.name: FormLabel
parts.note: htmlFor is supplied automatically. Turns text-destructive on error.

parts.name: FormControl
parts.note: A Slot. Wraps exactly one control and injects id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

parts.name: FormDescription
parts.note: Helper text, automatically referenced by aria-describedby

parts.name: FormMessage
parts.note: The validation error. Renders nothing when valid.

props.name: className
props.hint: Merged with the component classes via cn(). Use for layout only — never to override a variant that already exists.

keyboard: Enter submits from a single-line input
notes: This is the reason to use ui:form at all — the ARIA wiring is generated, not hand-written, so it cannot drift.
FormControl must wrap exactly one element. Two children breaks the Slot.
On failed submit, move focus to the first invalid field. react-hook-form does not do this for you.

forbiddenUsage: Parts used outside their required parent
Manual aria-invalid on a wrapped control
agentRules: The five parts are inseparable. Do not use FormLabel outside FormItem.
Never hand-write aria-describedby inside a form — you will fight the generated value.
Move focus to the first invalid field after a failed submit.

gaps: Does not move focus to the first invalid field on submit — implement that in your onInvalid handler.
